detail.longDescription:
#FeedEcho v1.48.0 is out. The RSS reader is now a full curation desk.

What changed:

Folders & OPML — Organize feeds into folders, import/export OPML with folder structure preserved (including file upload, finally), and get 4-way import feedback so you know what was skipped and why.

Compose — One dialog instead of a per-item popup. Write your own commentary, see live character counts per platform (Bluesky counts graphemes, not characters), cross-post to multiple destinations at once, and attach images with editable alt text. Your commentary ships verbatim, not parsed as a template.

Queue — Buffer for RSS. Schedule posts from the compose dialog, the scheduler dispatches them on a per-destination interval. There's a /queue page to reorder, edit, cancel, or post now.

Delivery badges in the reader — Every item shows what the cross-poster did with it: Echoed, Filtered, Queued, or Failed. Filtered items say which keyword matched. Click through to the delivery history for that specific item.

Mute from the reader — Select text in an article, hit Mute, and that phrase gets hidden across the feed (or all your feeds). Undo toast if you change your mind. Removable chips on the feeds page so the mute list is visible and editable.

Saved searches as smart feeds — Save any search query to your sidebar with a live unread count. Reopens with all operators intact (is:starred, feed:NAME, folder:NAME, in:title, in:body). Per-plan cap (3 trial, 20 paid).

Under the hood:
- Starred items are no longer deleted by retention pruning
- Keyset pagination replaces the hard 100-item limit
- 1,435 tests, dual SQLite/PostgreSQL, three CI jobs green

The reader is free in self-hosted mode and included in the paid plan on https://feedecho.net.

#RSS #opensource #selfhosted
